memories.author: D03
memories.text:
82-year-old male postal worker presents for routine review of allergic rhinitis and general health.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: He reports mild nasal congestion and sneezing, worse in the mornings, no fever or facial pain.

EXAMINATION: BP 138/82 mmHg, weight 68 kg, height 1.68 m giving BMI 24.1 (overweight). Nasal mucosa pale, turbinates slightly swollen. Lungs clear, cardiovascular regular.

IMPRESSION: Allergic rhinitis, controlled. Overweight (BMI 24.1) – advise reduced carbohydrate intake and daily walking. Lipids and glucose to be checked.

ARRANGEMENTS: Start cetirizine 10 mg HS, fluticasone nasal spray one spray each nostril OD. Review in 3 months. Return if: worsening blockage, facial pain, fever >39°C, or blood‑stained nasal discharge.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Cetirizine hydrochloride 10 mg tablet – take one tablet at night.
Fluticasone propionate nasal spray 50 mcg – one spray in each nostril once daily.
Review in 3 months.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Fasting lipid profile: Total cholesterol 5.2 mmol/L (ref <5.0), LDL 3.2 mmol/L (ref <2.6), HDL 1.1 mmol/L (ref >1.0), Triglycerides 1.8 mmol/L (ref <1.7).
Fasting blood glucose 6.1 mmol/L (ref 3.9-5.6).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
82-year-old male returns for allergic rhinitis follow‑up and weight check.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Nasal congestion improved but occasional itchy eyes; reports mild fatigue.

EXAMINATION: BP 140/84 mmHg, weight 69 kg, height 1.68 m => BMI 24.4 (overweight). Nasal mucosa less pale, mild turbinate hypertrophy. Lungs clear.

IMPRESSION: Allergic rhinitis partially controlled. Overweight persists – reinforce diet and activity advice. Consider adding montelukast.

ARRANGEMENTS: Continue cetirizine HS, fluticasone OD; add montelukast 10 mg HS. Review in 3 months. Return if: worsening symptoms, eye discharge, fever >39°C, or shortness of breath.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Cetirizine hydrochloride 10 mg tablet – take one tablet at night.
Fluticasone propionate nasal spray 50 mcg – one spray in each nostril once daily.
Montelukast sodium 10 mg tablet – take one tablet at night.
Review in 3 months.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Skin prick test positive for house dust mite (Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus) with wheal 6 mm; negative for pollen and pet dander. Total serum IgE 210 IU/mL (ref <100). Consistent with allergic rhinitis due to dust mite allergy.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
82-year-old male presents for routine review; notes persistent mild nasal blockage despite meds.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Nasal congestion worse at night, occasional post‑nasal drip; denies fever.

EXAMINATION: BP 142/86 mmHg, weight 68.5 kg, height 1.68 m => BMI 24.3 (overweight). Nasal mucosa slightly swollen, clear turbinates. Lungs clear, heart regular.

IMPRESSION: Allergic rhinitis inadequately controlled. Overweight (BMI 24.3) – advise diet and activity. Order baseline ECG given age and hypertension.

ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current meds; add saline nasal rinse BD. Order ECG. Review in 3 months. Influenza vaccine offered today – patient consents, vaccine given 02‑Oct‑2025. Return if: worsening blockage, facial pain, fever >39°C, or blood‑stained discharge.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Resting ECG: Sinus rhythm 72 bpm. No ST‑segment changes. Left ventricular voltage within normal limits. No arrhythmias. Normal study.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Refer to ENT specialist for evaluation of persistent allergic rhinitis symptoms despite maximal medical therapy. Consider possible nasal polyp or chronic sinusitis. Please assess and advise on further management.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: ENT report: Nasal endoscopy shows mild mucosal edema, no polyps. Sinus CT (limited) shows no sinusitis. Recommend continuing intranasal corticosteroid, consider allergen immunotherapy. No surgical intervention needed at this time.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Via clinic app: ‘Doctor, my nose feels stuffier again in the mornings and I’m sneezing more. The fluticasone spray seems less helpful. Should I increase the dose?’

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Cetirizine hydrochloride 10 mg tablet – take one tablet at night.
Fluticasone propionate nasal spray 50 mcg – increase to two sprays in each nostril once daily.
Montelukast sodium 10 mg tablet – take one tablet at night.
Review in 2 months.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
82-year-old male returns for annual review of allergic rhinitis and cardiovascular risk.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Nasal congestion improved after increasing fluticasone; occasional itchy eyes. Reports good energy.

EXAMINATION: BP 138/80 mmHg, weight 67 kg, height 1.68 m => BMI 23.7 (overweight). Nasal mucosa mildly pale, turbinates normal. Lungs clear.

IMPRESSION: Allergic rhinitis well controlled on current regimen. Overweight (BMI 23.7) – advise continued moderate activity and reduced refined carbs. Annual lipids and glucose checked.

ARRANGEMENTS: Continue cetirizine HS, fluticasone two sprays each nostril OD, montelukast HS. Review in 6 months. Influenza vaccine not due (given Oct 2025). Return if: worsening blockage, facial pain, fever >39°C, or blood‑stained discharge.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Fasting lipid profile: Total cholesterol 4.8 mmol/L (ref <5.0), LDL 2.9 mmol/L (ref <2.6), HDL 1.2 mmol/L (ref >1.0), Triglycerides 1.6 mmol/L (ref <1.7).
Fasting blood glucose 5.6 mmol/L (ref 3.9-5.6).
Total serum IgE 185 IU/mL (ref <100).
